previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic back pain, and anxiety was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia after eating contaminated food. Her blood glucose was 627 on admission but not in DKA. She improved with IV fluids, insulin, and antiemetics, and tolerated a regular diet without further vomiting. A gastric emptying study was normal, and blood cultures showed no infection. Her A1C was elevated at 12.8%, prompting adjustment of her insulin regimen to 28 units Lantus at bedtime and a revised carb-to-insulin ratio of 1:12 with correction scale of 1 unit Humalog per 40 points above 140. She expressed motivation to improve adherence and was connected with a new primary care provider, social work, and GI follow-up for esophageal varices and H. pylori eradication. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and close outpatient support planned.

___ y/o woman with DM1 and frequent admissions for

but has previous diagnosis of gastroparesis. She continues on

which was attributed to overtreating high readings with humalog 
throughout the night. During this current admission, LFTs and 
lipase are within normal limits. Patient also underwent CT 
abdomen and pelvis without acute process. Does not appear to 
have infectious precipitant to her elevated BG. Overall, her 
prior anion gap has closed with IVF and without insulin gtt in

Her diet was slowly advanced to regulars and she was discharged 
with a new insulin regimen (sliding scale provided - see ___ 
note in OMR, and 24 units of glargine QHS).  She received a 
total of 5L of NS, did see the nutritionist, and outpatient f/u 
was set up with both PCP, ___, as well as psychiatry.

# Acute renal failure: likely related to dehydration and 
inadequate fluid intake combined with ACEi use. No new 
medications or NSAIDs. Improved after aggressive IVF.  
Lisinopril was restarted at time of discharge.

# Social issues: Numerous admissions and long history of 
depression/anxiety, non-compliance, and chronic pain. She has 
had difficulty keeping outpatient appointments with GI, PCP, 
___, pain clinic, and ___ though social work had been 
trying to establish a multidisciplinary care team for her.  It 
was clear to the primary team during this admission that social 
factors do indeed play a big role in her multiple presentations 
to the hospital.  Social work was consulted and with their 
assistance, she was set up to see a therapist at ___ 
as an outpatient.  In speaking with the endocrinology team, they 
also feel that her insulin can be titrated often, but until her 
social situation is more adequately addressed, she will 
unfortunately be someone who may present with a similar story 
repeatedly.  There have been efforts to also have her see the 
Pharmacist in ___ (her primary care clinic here at ___ and 
her PCP is very involved in her care.  Communication was 
maintained with her PCP throughout her hospitalization in an 
effort to adequately address issues both in and out of house.  

# Anxiety/depression: Pt has been seen by outpatient psychiatry 
who feels that her frequent presentations may actually be 
precipitated often by anxiety playing a role. She is not 
currently on much in terms of anxiolytics, however given the 
nausea, and one episode of acute anxiety, ativan was started prn 
in house.  Notably, she did not use any ativan while here.  As 
above, psychiatry f/u was attempted to be set up, however the 
patient will need to call the office as per their 
preference/protocol.  As above, she was set up with ___ 
counseling services as an outpatient with an appointment, and a 
discharge summary was sent to them.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST RADIOGRAPH PERFORMED ON ___

Comparison is made with a prior chest radiograph from ___.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Back pain, abdominal pain, fever, assess for pneumonia.

FINDINGS:  PA and lateral views of the chest are obtained.  The lungs are
clear bilaterally without focal consolidation, effusion, or pneumothorax. 
Cardiomediastinal silhouette is normal.  No free air below the right
hemidiaphragm.  Bony structures are intact.

IMPRESSION:  Normal chest radiograph.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with h/o diabetes, gastroparesis, abdominal
pain, nausea, vomiting and fevers; evaluate for abscess.

COMPARISON:  CT of the abdomen and pelvis from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT  images were acquired through the abdomen and pelvis.  The IV
infiltrated during IV contrast administration and approximately 30cc was
successfully delivered and approximately 20 ml infiltrated into the patient's
wrist. Imaging was delayed post contrast administration and due to poor IV
access, no additional IV contrast was given. Multiplanar reformations were
generated.

LUNG BASES:  The imaged lung bases are clear.  

ABDOMEN: Please note, due to lack of contrast enhancement, evaluation of solid
organs is limited. The liver, spleen, both adrenals, and gallbladder are
unremarkable.  Both kidneys show normal excretion of contrast with no 
perinephric stranding.  There is no gastric distension.

No abdominal, retroperitoneal or mesenteric lymphadenopathy by CT size
criteria is present.  No abdominal free fluid or free air is present.  The
small and large bowel are unremarkable.

PELVIS: The rectum, sigmoid colon, bladder, uterus, and both adnexa are
unremarkable.  The patient has a pessary in place.

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES: Normal.

IMPRESSION: No acute intra-abdominal process. 

Please note, evaluation is limited due to delay in imaging post administration
of approximately 30cc IV contrast. Infiltration of approximately 20 cc
contrast into the wrist.
